transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (CortexHead of ML), Tom Reynolds (Cortex Eng Manager), Aisha Khan (Cortex Security), Ben Carter (PM), Speaker 1

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy): Discussed POC acceptance tests and sign-off thresholds. Defined go/no-go metrics: latency (p50/p95), throughput, accuracy/QA thresholds for hallucination, embedding recall, cost per 1K tokens, and reporting format (CSV/JSON + dashboard). Agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for making time, good to see you. quick call purpose — lock down the acceptance tests for the POC so both teams sign off on go/no-go thresholds.
[00:18] Priya Menon: thanks lena, yeah this is important for us. we want clear pass/fail criteria — not fuzzy "looks good". our legal/security folks will also require a reproducible report.
[00:34] Diego Alvarez: totally. hi, i'm diego, i'll run the benchmark harness and help with configs. i can share templates for latency/throughput and evaluation scripts.
[00:45] Tom Reynolds: quick note — our prod-ish workload is chat-like Q&A and a separate embeddings pipeline for search relevance. both need coverage in the acceptance tests.
[01:02] Aisha Khan: and from security i need to know how logs are stored, whether tokens leave our VPC in the private pilot, and kms integration. also retention windows.
[01:18] Lena Park: understood. we'll cover both workloads. diego, can you outline the concrete metrics we propose?
[01:26] Diego Alvarez: sure. i'll read them out then we can iterate:
[01:30] - Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms for generation requests at 40 concurrent sessions (approx 80 rps).
[01:46] - Throughput: sustain 1000 tokens/sec aggregate across the cluster for the chat workload with our suggested batching policy.
[01:58] - Accuracy/quality: for the 3 canonical prompt sets, >= 92% match to expected answers using fuzzy-match rubric (we'll share rubric).
[02:11] - Hallucination threshold: less than 3% of outputs flagged as hallucinations by the rubric and manual spot-checking.
[02:24] - Embedding recall: top-5 recall >= 88% vs. your internal benchmark for the search snapshots.
[02:36] - Cost: cost per 1k tokens during test should not exceed $0.70 (hosted) or equivalent run-rate on dedicated.
[02:47] - Stability: no more than 2% error rate (5xx / total requests) during a 30-minute sustained run.
[03:00] - Rollback criteria: if latency p95 degrades >30% compared to baseline or hallucination >5% we consider immediate fail and investigate.

[03:15] Priya Menon: couple of questions — the accuracy metric, is 92% strict? also our expected answers sometimes have multiple acceptable variants.
[03:27] Diego Alvarez: good point. our plan is to use a tiered acceptance:
[03:31] - Tier 1 (hard pass): >=92% exact/fuzzy match as defined in rubric (automated), AND hallucination <3%.
[03:42] - Tier 2 (conditional pass): 88-91% with manual review of flagged cases and agreement on remediation list.
[03:51] - Fail: <88% or hallucination >5%.

[04:00] Ben Carter: for the embeddings recall, how do you compute recall? is that cosine threshold or a labeled dataset?
[04:09] Diego Alvarez: we use labeled queries + ground-truth doc ids. compute top-k recall at k=5 using cosine similarity on 1536-d vectors (or whatever model dims). we provide scripts to reproduce.
[04:22] Tom Reynolds: this matches our internal tests. what about sequence length distributions? our chat median is ~220 tokens, 95th percentile ~980 tokens for long context scenarios.
[04:35] Diego Alvarez: perfect — we'll run two profile buckets: short (<=256), long (256-1000). batching configs will adapt; we'll show impact on latency.

[04:50] Speaker 1: uh small interruption, sorry, is there an SLA requirement for the POC or just acceptance?
[04:56] Lena Park: for POC it's acceptance-specific; we do provide rough availability expectations but production SLA conversation comes after.

[05:05] Aisha Khan: on data protection — if we run on Redwood Private in our VPC, will tokens ever route outside? and how are logs written?
[05:15] Diego Alvarez: for Private, control plane talks to your control network; inference happens in your VPC. logs can be sent to your SIEM via TLS, and we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK). we'll share the network diagram and exact logging granularity.
[05:32] Aisha Khan: ok please include retention options (30/90/365 days) and a flag for PII redaction in logs.

[05:40] Lena Park: noted. back to acceptance tests — reporting format. we propose three delivery artifacts:
[05:47] - Raw run artifact: CSV with per-request latencies, tokens, error codes.
[05:54] - Aggregated report: JSON summary with p50/p90/p95, throughput, cost estimate, and pass/fail per metric.
[06:03] - Console dashboard snapshot: PNGs and a shared dashboard link with drilldowns.

[06:12] Priya Menon: the CSV is important for our data team. can you make column headers standard? timestamp, req_id, user_id (hashed), model, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code, response_score?
[06:25] Diego Alvarez: yep that's our default schema. we'll add a response_score field (0-1) for automated heuristic on hallucination and a manual_review flag.

[06:35] Tom Reynolds: what about reproducibility? we need seeds, model versions, hardware details, kernel/compilation flags.
[06:43] Diego Alvarez: we'll include model hash, runtime version, kernel flags, CUDA/cuDNN versions, GPU type, and batch settings in the report header. also commit hash for the test harness.

[06:55] Priya Menon: timeline check — what's realistic? our target is to have acceptance sign-off by end of April.
[07:03] Lena Park: workable. proposed timeline:
[07:06] - This week: exchange rubrics, workload snapshots (your side) and test harness (ours).
[07:12] - Week of 2025-03-24: run dry-run benchmarks (internal, low load) and review results with you.
[07:20] - Week of 2025-03-31: 2-hour formal acceptance run with your stakeholders observing.
[07:27] - First week of April: remediation window for any issues found.
[07:32] - Target final sign-off by 2025-04-25.

[07:38] Aisha Khan: if anything fails, what is the dispute process? do we retest?
[07:44] Lena Park: we'll do an agreed remediation plan. if a Hard Pass metric fails, we'll triage, implement fixes (config changes, quantization changes, routing), then rerun acceptance within the remediation window. both parties agree on re-run conditions recorded in the acceptance doc.

[07:59] Ben Carter: can we have a go/no-go checklist in the report header so reviewers can get an at-a-glance result?
[08:06] Diego Alvarez: yes — we'll include a pass/fail table with each metric, observed value, threshold, and note. also a root-cause field for any failing metric.

[08:18] Priya Menon: what about A/B tests vs canary? for POC we just want single-run baseline, right?
[08:24] Lena Park: correct — POC acceptance is single-run baseline. later we can set up canaries for gradual rollouts.

[08:32] Tom Reynolds: some practical items — our infra team needs the Jenkins job and k6 script to be idempotent. we don't want to run a script that modifies state.
[08:42] Diego Alvarez: our harness is "read-only workload" by default; any write workloads will be mocked or run against a sandbox. we will label test runs as "read-only workload" in the header.

[08:53] Aisha Khan: for the security review, i'll need SOC2 docs and the control plane/network diagram. also is there an on-prem option?
[09:01] Lena Park: yes, Private supports on-prem containerized installs for air-gapped environments — that's a heavier lift, but possible. i'll send SOC2 attestation and network diagram after the call.

[09:13] Speaker 1: (muffled) uh will the cost estimate reflect burst pricing or sustained?
[09:18] Diego Alvarez: cost figure in the report will show both sustained run-rate and burst cost assumptions with billing model. we'll include a per-1k token rate and assumed tokenization distribution.

[09:29] Priya Menon: acceptance rubric: can you show an example of the fuzzy-match scoring? we need to see how you count partial credit.
[09:36] Diego Alvarez: example — normalized token-level overlap + semantic similarity using BLEURT-like score. we'll attach the scoring script so you can run locally.

[09:48] Tom Reynolds: are there any known headroom expectations — e.g., if we double concurrency does p95 jump by 2x? we need to know where tipping points are.
[09:58] Diego Alvarez: we'll include a headroom chart from the bench runs showing latency vs concurrency and throughput curves. that helps determine autoscale thresholds.

[10:09] Ben Carter: on sign-off, who signs? is it Priya or someone in infra?
[10:14] Priya Menon: i'll own the ML criteria sign-off; tom will own infra/perf sign-off; aisha will sign security acceptance. product can be ben for final business sign-off.

[10:24] Lena Park: perfect. i'll document the acceptance signatories in the draft and circulate.

[10:30] Diego Alvarez: small note — for embedding evals we recommend at least 10K query-doc pairs to get stable recall measurements. smaller samples can be noisy.
[10:40] Priya Menon: we can provide 12K.

[10:44] Aisha Khan: red team / adversarial tests — do you include fuzzing for prompt injection in the acceptance?
[10:51] Diego Alvarez: we recommend a subset of adversarial prompts as part of the security checklist. for POC acceptance, we'll run a curated set and flag any failures; if severe, that becomes hard-fail.

[11:03] Tom Reynolds: how long will the formal acceptance run take? you said a 2-hour block — is that representative?
[11:08] Diego Alvarez: yes, 2 hours for the formal run plus a 30-minute pre-check and 30-minute post-run review; total 3 hours booked in calendar.

[11:19] Priya Menon: documentation — we'll need the raw outputs and a reproducible script to re-run the acceptance if required.
[11:26] Lena Park: absolutely. all artifacts will be committed to a shared repo and tagged with run id and commit hash.

[11:33] Ben Carter: ok let's recap quick and owners.
[11:36] Lena Park: recap: acceptance metrics and tiers as diego outlined; reporting schema (CSV, JSON summary, dashboard); timeline to target sign-off 2025-04-25; deliverables: harness, rubric, network/security docs. owners: diego prepares harness; priya provides workloads; aisha security checklist; lena sends acceptance doc.

[11:56] Priya Menon: i just want to add that in conditional pass cases we'll need an explicit remediation acceptance test plan.
[12:03] Lena Park: yes we'll include remediation acceptance criteria and re-run windows in the document.

[12:12] Tom Reynolds: two final items — confirm that the test will include both hosted and dedicated config numbers (if we run on Redwood-hosted and on dedicated nodes).
[12:21] Diego Alvarez: yes, we'll run both or equivalent model variants and include a channel breakdown. where dedicated isn't available in the timeframe we'll simulate with same hardware profiles and note assumptions.

[12:33] Aisha Khan: and please include an artifact that lists what data leaves our systems, even if encrypted (for legal).
[12:40] Lena Park: noted. we'll include a data flow appendix.

[12:47] Lena Park: any other questions?
[12:50] Ben Carter: none from me. thanks everyone.
[12:53] Priya Menon: thanks, lena. looking forward to the draft.
[12:57] Speaker 1: (off) thanks.
[12:59] Diego Alvarez: i'll share the bench config and a sample run this Friday.
[13:04] Lena Park: great. we'll follow up with the doc and action items. thanks all.

End of transcript.
